answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The zenith multiplier is published, charged in saffron, and sparrow lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4246 identities would post 4252 proofs and burn roughly 57 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
